title: Sixteen Visits and One Loose Tooth
subtitle: 健康与医疗 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 健康与医疗（生活与学习·健康的生活方式与医疗）
meta: 主题语境：健康与医疗（生活与学习·健康的生活方式与医疗）　|　核心词汇：dentist　|　正文 335 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dentist 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 my mother ① found a dentist that no family in the street would have trusted, and she said the finding was the whole of the winter. The ② dentist, meaning the practitioner and not the surgery, came sixteen visits and stayed unregistered; a dentist, she said, is the only thing in a street that is judged by how long he is left unvisited.

Every ③ dentist in that street had the same loose tooth in the bowl, and the ④ dentist at the end, meaning the one who came on Saturdays and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever recommended twice. A dentist, my grandmother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to sit; my mother said the sitting is the part that fills sixteen visits.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the dentist was the whole of the treatment, meaning the surgery and not the practitioner. The ⑥ dentist, meaning the surgery and not any of that, is the only thing in a treatment that everybody books and nobody enjoys; dentist, he said, is either somebody you find or the only word that means both a practitioner and a surgery. He said the surgery is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ dentist had become a line in a card, and the card had become an argument about the loose tooth. The ⑧ dentist of the whole thing, my mother wrote in March, was one street and sixteen visits of sitting; dentist, she said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to sit. She said the sitting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ dentist I remember is the one at the end, who last came in 1976 and is still described as the gentlest in the street. A ⑩ dentist, my grandmother said in 1978, is the only one who improves by being visited; every dentist, she said, is a surgery that has agreed to look like a practitioner. She said the surgery was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 牙医（指那条街上开业的那一位）
B. n. 牙医（指那位执业者本人，与那间诊所相对）
C. 固定搭配：find a dentist 找到一位牙医
D. n. 牙医（指周六出诊的那一位）
E. n. 牙医；齿科（抽象总称，指一条街上的看牙之事）
F. n. 牙医（指病历卡上写到、被登记的那一位）
G. n. 牙科诊所（指治疗时预约的那间诊室）
H. n. 诊所（抽象总称，指人人预约却无人乐意的那个去处）

items.q: found a dentist that no family in the street would have trusted

answers.why: find a dentist 意为“找到一位牙医”，1954 年母亲找到了一位那条街上没有一家人肯信任的牙医。
dentist 意为“牙医”，指那位执业者本人而不是那间诊所，他来了十六次而始终没有注册。
dentist 意为“牙医”，指那条街上开业的每一位牙医，每一位的碗里都有同一颗松动的牙。
dentist 意为“牙医”，指周六出诊的那一位，是唯一有人推荐过两次的。
dentist 意为“牙科诊所”，指治疗时预约的那间诊室，叔叔说这间诊所就是那次治疗的全部。
dentist 意为“诊所”，指人人预约却无人乐意的那个去处而不是那位执业者，是治疗里人人都预约、却无人乐意的东西。
dentist 意为“牙医”，指病历卡上写到、被登记的那一位，到 1962 年这位牙医成了病历卡上的一行。
dentist 意为“牙医、齿科”，母亲三月写道，整件事的看牙之事是一条街和十六次的坐诊。
dentist 意为“牙医”，我记得的是末尾那一位，1976 年最后一次来，至今仍被说成街上最温和的。
dentist 为抽象总称，祖母 1978 年说，一位牙医是唯一会因为被上门求诊而变得更好的人。
